checked_ok: Ticket accounting: PostToMainThread and RunOnMainThread both push the task and increment main_tasks_queued under main_task_mutex, so ticket order equals queue order. DrainMainThreadTasks swaps out the whole queue and adds exactly the number of tasks it ran. So a waiter cannot return before its own task has run, and a posted task cannot make it wait forever. Only the old condition remains: the main loop never drains.

Title slot: title_text and title_queued are touched only under title_mutex. The posted task clears title_queued and copies the text before SDL_SetWindowTitle, so a newer UpdateTitle posts again and cannot be lost. The drain swap drops no task. Switching titleasync 1 to 0 or 0 to 1 mid-run keeps FIFO order: a pending post runs before the sync task, so the newest text wins. The flag cannot stick at true while the main loop runs.

Lifetime: posted closures live in WindowContext::main_tasks and run only from WindowContext::Run. Swapchain recreation recreates only the surface, never the SDL_Window or the WindowContext. Normal exit is std::quick_exit, and graphics has no emergency-shutdown hook, so ~WindowContext never runs with a closure pending. Destroying a pending std::function does not run it.

Lock order: title_mutex and main_task_mutex are never held together. The present thread takes VideoOutConfig::mutex, then title_mutex (released), then main_task_mutex (released), then SDL's queue lock. The main thread takes title_mutex inside the task with no other emulator lock held. No new cycle.

SDL_PushEvent from the present thread is thread-safe in SDL2 and is the same call RunOnMainThread already made on every present. The wake is a bare SDL_USEREVENT, the same type as the overlay visibility event (the first SDL_RegisterEvents id). ProcessSystemOverlayInput takes it as a wake: it pops a pending update early, or returns true on an empty queue. This existed before, and nothing is lost.

ReserveFlipRequest: both ways of taking the lock (TryLock succeeds, or TryLock fails and Lock follows) are followed at once by the ReserveUnlock RAII bound to the same Common::Mutex. The three returns after it each unlock exactly once. The early returns before it take nothing. Common::Mutex is recursive (CRITICAL_SECTION or std::recursive_mutex), so for the owner TryLock behaves like Lock, and the contended path still spins inside EnterCriticalSection as before.

Default titleasync=0: behaviour is the same as before the patch. The only additions per present are a knob load, two rdtsc reads and two FrameStats Adds (no-ops unless tracing). The stall test is inert without the variable.

Knob tables: TitleAsync is the last row both in enum Knob and in KNOB_DEFINITIONS {KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC, titleasync, 0, 1}. The knob is read on the present thread, and Gates::Poll writes it on the same thread. build114a.log says BUILD OK.

The positive control can tell the two values apart once the main loop runs. At titleasync 0 the sleep task is queued before the title task that waits, inside FlipQueue::Flip's hold of VideoOutConfig::mutex, so GuestGpu blocks in ReserveFlipRequest for about the sleep length. At titleasync 1, on Windows, nothing on the present path waits for the main thread (RecreateSurface uses RunOnMainThread only on Apple).

info.title: The stall frame counts UpdateTitle calls, not flips, and at titleasync 1 from the environment it runs ahead during boot
info.failure: frame_num is UpdateTitle's own static counter. It counts blank, pause-repeat and overlay-refresh presents. It skips presents made while the preparation overlay is up and presents that fail after two retries. It is not flip_status.count. At titleasync 0 the boot park allows only one call before WindowRun. At titleasync 1 set from the environment, the present thread counts blank presents at 60 Hz through the whole boot. So KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST=3000:3000 fires at a different game moment in the two seal-01 entries. A scorer that looks for the stall in the row 'FrameTrace: n=3000' reads the wrong row.
info.fix: Locate the stall by the position of the 'MainStallTest: queued' line in the log, or log flip_status.count with it. Set titleasync for both control entries the same way (gate file for both, or environment for both).

info.title: main_tasks_run is counted per batch, so a posted task later in a batch delays earlier RunOnMainThread waiters
info.failure: DrainMainThreadTasks adds tasks.size() only after every task in the swapped batch has run. Say a RunOnMainThread task with ticket T and a later PostToMainThread task (such as a long sleep) end up in the same batch. The waiter for T then also waits for the later task, although its own task finished long before. This does not affect the planned control: the sleep is queued before the title task that waits. On Windows, UpdateTitle is the only waiter today (RecreateSurface waits only on Apple).
info.fix: Optional: after each task, increment main_tasks_run and SignalAll under the lock, or signal per ticket.

finding.title: titleasync=1 at process start stops the present thread's startup park, so two threads can run Presenter::Present at once
finding.location: src/graphics/presentation/window/window.cpp:1133-1151 (post branch) together with window.cpp:966-971 (WindowPrepareShaders presents on the main thread), videoOut.cpp:259 (the present thread starts at Graphics::Initialize), videoOut.cpp:~840-875 (overlay-refresh and blank presents), swapchain.cpp:579-600 and :737 (AcquireNextImage and m_frame_index with no lock), videoOut.cpp:1190 (Gates::Poll runs only on guest flips)

Its first loop iterations do a blank present (no video out is open yet, and total_wait < 0 after the sleep overshoots). The preparation overlay is still off, so Present calls UpdateTitle, then RunOnMainThread. The main thread is not in Run() yet (it is in InitAll, LoadElf, then WindowPrepareShaders), so the present thread stays parked until the first DrainMainThreadTasks in WindowRun. That park is the only thing that keeps the present thread out of Presenter::Present while WindowPrepareShaders presents from the main thread every ~16 ms. At titleasync 1, set from the environment (KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC=1) or as the planned shipped default: the first UpdateTitle returns at once and the present thread keeps looping. Once SetShaderPreparationOverlay(true) is set, GetSystemOverlayVisualState reports active, so NeedsSystemOverlayRefresh is true and the present thread calls PrepareLastFrame or PrepareBlankFrame, then Present, on every vblank. The main thread presents at the same time. Swapchain::AcquireNextImage runs outside every lock. Both threads read the same m_frame_index. Both call vkAcquireNextImageKHR on the same swapchain with the same m_image_acquired[f], which breaks Vulkan's external-synchronization rule and the rule that the semaphore has no pending signal. m_image_index gets overwritten between acquire and RecordPresentCommands. Two submits wait on one binary-semaphore signal. Possible results: the wrong image is presented, the GPU hangs or the device is lost, or EXIT on vkQueuePresentKHR. Warm runs have a preparation window of about 20-120 ms, so the race is intermittent. A cold or prepare-cold run keeps the window open for seconds. Neither seal can see this. A gate-file or schedule arm is applied first by Gates::Poll in FlipQueue::Flip, at the first guest flip. That is after WindowRun has already released the parked thread. finding.fix: Serialize Presenter::Present, for example with a present mutex from AcquireNextImage through swapchain.Present and Release. Or have PresentThread skip presenting while ShaderPreparationOverlayActive(), because the main thread owns presenting then. Before shipping titleasync=1, run one entry with KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC=1 set in the environment and with a real preparation phase (prepare-cold or a long precache).

One thread can also overwrite m_image_index between another's acquire and its RecordPresentCommands or present. FramePool locking (swapchain.cpp:103-180) protects only frame ownership.

I could not refute this. Each step of the failure sequence matches the code.

1. The present thread starts early. Graphics::Initialize (agc.cpp:64-65) calls WindowInit and then VideoOutInit, and VideoOutDriver::Impl starts m_present_thread (videoOut.cpp:259). This is the last subsystem that Init brings up. After it, the main thread runs InitAll, then LoadElf, then Execute. Execute calls WindowPrepareShaders and only then WindowRun (emulator.cpp:186-197, 250-255).

2. Its first loop iterations reach a blank present. loop.paused starts false (windowInternal.h WindowLoopState). No video out is open, and total_wait goes negative once a sleep overshoots, so it calls PrepareBlankFrame and then Present (videoOut.cpp:860-873). The preparation overlay is still false (systemOverlay.cpp:476-484), so the check at swapchain.cpp:903 (`if (!preparing) UpdateTitle()`) calls UpdateTitle.

3. At titleasync 0, UpdateTitle calls RunOnMainThread (window.cpp:772-794). That call waits until main_tasks_run reaches its ticket. main_tasks_run is only advanced by DrainMainThreadTasks, and the only caller of that is Run() (window.cpp:834). WindowPrepareShaders never drains the queue. So the present thread stays parked through all of WindowPrepareShaders.

4. At titleasync 1, UpdateTitle calls PostToMainThread and returns at once. The knob comes from the environment at first use (gates.cpp:421-431), so KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC=1 is in effect from the very first present.

5. During preparation the present thread keeps presenting. GetSystemOverlayVisualState returns active=true while g_shader_preparation is set (systemOverlay.cpp:467-468). That makes NeedsSystemOverlayRefresh true, so the present thread calls PrepareLastFrame and Present every vblank (videoOut.cpp:841-856). At the same moment the main thread presents every ~16 ms from WindowPrepareShaders (window.cpp:968-971).

6. Nothing serializes Presenter::Present across threads. FramePool's m_mutex only covers frame ownership. The renderer mutex only covers recording and submit. queue_mutex only covers presentKHR. Swapchain::AcquireNextImage (swapchain.cpp:579-600) runs outside every lock, and so do the reads and writes of m_frame_index, m_image_index and m_acquire_ticks (swapchain.cpp:700-705, 737). That allows:
   - two concurrent vkAcquireNextImageKHR calls on the same swapchain, which violates Vulkan's external-synchronization rule;
   - a second acquire on a semaphore that already has a pending signal;
   - m_image_index being overwritten between acquire and RecordPresentCommands;
   - a submit that waits on an m_image_acquired[f+1] that nothing will signal.

7. Overlap is likely in practice. The harness runs with --present-mode Fifo (run.sh). The two threads together ask for about twice the vblank rate, so acquire blocks, and a blocked acquire is exactly when the other thread walks into it. The window is real even in warm runs: the current logs show "ShaderPreparation: startup wait finished in 75 ms" and "72 ms", roughly 4-5 vblanks. In prepare-cold the window lasts seconds.

8. The seals cannot see it. Common::Gates::Poll is called only from FlipQueue::Flip on a guest flip (videoOut.cpp:1190, the only call site). A gate-file or schedule value of titleasync=1 is therefore applied only after WindowRun has already released the parked thread, so every boot in those arms starts at titleasync 0. Only KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC=1 in the environment, or a shipped default of 1, reaches the startup path, and nothing in the plan measures that.

Two limits on the claim:
- The patch's default is 0, so the defect is latent today. It only matters once the knob is 1 at process start.
- The root cause, an unserialized Presenter::Present, predates the patch. At titleasync 0 it is hidden only by the accidental startup park.

Even so, the gates.h comment calls the knob "safe at any moment", and the plan is to ship it as the default. At that default the race can bring wrong-image presents, a GPU hang or device loss, or an EXIT during startup, and the planned control cannot detect it. That justifies MAJOR.

finding.title: Every run that boots at titleasync 0 logs a boot-time MainThreadWait line (frame=1), even an entry meant to be titleasync 1
finding.failure: The present thread's first UpdateTitle waits in RunOnMainThread from roughly the first vblank after VideoOutInit until WindowRun starts. That covers LoadElf and all of shader preparation, often seconds. When it returns, title_ns is at least 50 ms, so it prints 'MainThreadWait: us=<boot length> frame=1 titleasync=0' and uses up one of the 32 slots. The knob is applied from the gate file only at the first guest flip. So if seal 01's titleasync=1 entry sets the knob that way, it still boots at 0 and prints the same line. A scorer that reads 'no MainThreadWait in the titleasync=1 entry' as the control's pass condition would FAIL a working fix. A scorer that reads 'a MainThreadWait line exists' as proof the titleasync=0 stall fired would PASS even when the stall test never fired. The same boot wait also lands in pres_title_ns. It is folded into the first FrameTrace baseline, so no row shows it, but any total taken from process start includes it.
finding.fix: Score only lines with frame equal to the MainStallTest frame and us close to the stall length. Or skip the log and the counter until the main loop has started, for example with a flag set in Run() before the first DrainMainThreadTasks.

I could not refute this. The code supports every step of the failure sequence.

1. The present thread starts at boot. Graphics::Initialize (agc.cpp:64-65) calls VideoOutInit, and the Impl constructor starts PresentThread (videoOut.cpp:259) inside Emulator::Init. That happens long before Execute, WindowPrepareShaders and WindowRun (emulator.cpp:186-198, 228-253). `loop.paused` defaults to false (windowInternal.h:31). With no video-out handle open, PresentThread presents a blank frame as soon as total_wait < 0 (videoOut.cpp:858-873), which is about the second 60 Hz tick. It can also present at :841-856 if the overlay needs a refresh.

2. Presenter::Present calls UpdateTitle whenever `!preparing` (swapchain.cpp:903). `preparing` is ShaderPreparationOverlayActive(), which is set only inside WindowPrepareShaders (window.cpp:968). So a blank present during Init, PipelinePrecache, InitAll or LoadElf reaches UpdateTitle with frame_num = 1 (the static counter, window.cpp:1081/1095).

3. At titleasync 0 that call goes into RunOnMainThread (window.cpp:1153), which waits for `main_tasks_run >= ticket` (:787-790). DrainMainThreadTasks is called only from WindowContext::Run (:834). WindowPrepareShaders pumps SDL events but never drains the tasks. So the wait lasts until WindowRun starts. In the last real log, PipelinePrecache took 205 ms and shader preparation took 75 ms, and LoadElf came on top of that. The wait is therefore far above 50 ms, and window.cpp:1158-1164 prints `MainThreadWait: us=<boot> frame=1 titleasync=0`, using one of the 32 slots.

4. The knob is read on every call, from Gates::Value. From the environment (KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC) it is set at Gates::Initialize, i.e. at the first access (gates.cpp:421-433). From a gate file or a schedule it is applied only by Gates::Poll, and Poll is called only on a guest flip (videoOut.cpp:1190). The harness normally passes knobs through KYTY_GATE_FILE (gen_gates/enter_scene). A titleasync=1 entry configured that way still boots at 0 and prints the same frame=1 line. That entry also still waits during boot, which is harmless.

Why MINOR and not higher: there is no behaviour change at the default and no deadlock. The pre-registered control prediction in ROADMAP §114 item 2(3) is based on the frame row's dt ≈ M and on GpuWaitSlow, not on MainThreadWait lines. So the planned scorer is not necessarily broken. Still, the instrument deterministically emits a false "main thread busy" line in every titleasync-0 run, and in gate-file titleasync-1 runs. Any scorer or reader that counts MainThreadWait lines, or treats their presence or absence as proof, is misled. The same boot wait is also added to pres_title_ns. The fix the reviewer proposes (match frame == MainStallTest frame and us ≈ M, or arm the log and counter only after Run() starts) is appropriate.

I could not refute this. The code confirms each step of the failure sequence.

1. **The present thread presents from boot, before WindowRun.** `agc.cpp:64-65` runs `WindowInit` and then `VideoOutInit` inside `Init()` (emulator.cpp `Run`), before `LoadElf`. The `VideoOutDriver::Impl` constructor starts `PresentThread` (`videoOut.cpp:259`). In `PresentThread` (`videoOut.cpp:806-880`), `total_wait` goes negative after almost every sleep: the sleep time is rounded up, then the time actually slept is subtracted. So with no video-out handle open (`any_open` false, which holds until the guest runs), it presents a blank frame about every vblank (`videoOut.cpp:871-872`).

2. **That present calls UpdateTitle.** `Presenter::Present` calls `UpdateTitle` when `!preparing` (`swapchain.cpp:844,903`). `ShaderPreparationOverlayActive()` becomes true only inside the `WindowPrepareShaders` loop (`window.cpp:968`). During `InitAll`/`LoadElf` it is false, so the first boot blank present calls `UpdateTitle` with `frame_num = 1`.

3. **The wait is unbounded until Run.** At titleasync 0, `RunOnMainThread` (`window.cpp:772-791`) queues the task and waits until `main_tasks_run >= ticket`. Only `DrainMainThreadTasks` advances that count. Its only caller is `WindowContext::Run` (`window.cpp:834`), reached from `WindowRun` after `WindowPrepareShaders` (`emulator.cpp:186-197`). `WindowPrepareShaders` only calls `SDL_PollEvent` and never drains the queue. The present thread therefore waits through the rest of `LoadElf` plus all of shader preparation. The current logs show `ShaderPreparation: startup wait finished in 72/75 ms` for that step alone, which already exceeds the 50 ms threshold. The line `MainThreadWait: us=<boot> frame=1 titleasync=0` is printed (`window.cpp:1158-1164`) and uses one of the 32 slots. `NowNs` works without `KYTY_FRAME_TRACE` (`frameStats.cpp:198`), so the line appears in every run.

4. **A gate-file setting of 1 still boots at 0.** Knobs are initialised from environment variables only (`gates.cpp:421-445`; fallback 0). The gate file and the schedule are applied only through `Gates::Poll`, which is called after the first guest flip's present (`videoOut.cpp:1190`). An entry that sets `titleasync=1` through `KYTY_GATE_FILE` (the harness convention) therefore also prints the boot line, stamped `titleasync=0`. Only `KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC=1` in the environment would suppress it.

**Mitigation.** The line does carry the field `titleasync=0` and `frame=1`, so a careful scorer can filter it out. The ROADMAP prediction for seal 01 is written in terms of a FrameTrace frame with dt ≈ M and `GpuWaitSlow`, not `MainThreadWait` lines. No seal or scorer exists yet.

**Severity.** The boot wait blocks nothing: the blank path holds neither the render mutex nor the cfg mutex. So this is an instrument or control-interpretation hazard, not wrong emulator behaviour. It is also a real reproducible artifact in every run. MINOR, as claimed.

checked_ok: The old path is unchanged at titleasync=0: RunOnMainThread gets the same lambda [this, text=std::move(text)]{SDL_SetWindowTitle(...)} (window.cpp:1153). RunOnMainThread and DrainMainThreadTasks are unchanged (window.cpp:772-794, 808-823). PostToMainThread is never called at the default (the knob is 0 and the stall-test pair is {0,0}).

The stall_test static init is harmless at the default. With the variable absent, getenv returns null, there is no LOGF, and v = {0,0}, so stall_test.second != 0 is false forever. Init runs once, as a thread-safe function-local static, on the present thread only (the only caller is swapchain.cpp:903).

NowNs on the present thread adds no new one-time cost. The 20 ms TSC calibration (frameStats.cpp:142-155) has already run before the first present, because NowNs is called unconditionally on the submit path (commandScheduler.cpp:911), in vma.cpp:354 and in hostImport.cpp:91. Each call costs one rdtsc and one double divide. FrameStats::Add returns at once when g_count_limit is 0 (no trace), or for index >= LogNs under fslean. At the default the added cost is well under 1 us per present.

The ReserveFlipRequest TryLock is equivalent to the old LockGuard. On success, TryEnterCriticalSection gives one acquisition, as before (or recursive_mutex::try_lock off Windows). On failure it falls back to the same Lock(). The RAII ReserveUnlock unlocks on all three returns. FlipQueue::Reserve takes only m_mutex and does no CondVar wait on the config mutex, so the recursion depth is the same.

No new lock-order hazard. AttachShard on first Add from a guest or GuestGpu thread takes the FrameStats registry mutex while holding VideoOutConfig::mutex. The present thread already reads counters under the config mutex (FS::Read, videoOut.cpp:1249), and no registry-mutex holder ever takes the config mutex.

Knob tables are aligned. check_gate_order.py (read-only run) reports Knob 32 enum entries / 32 rows and Gate 111/111, 'GATE ORDER: clean'. TitleAsync <-> titleasync match exactly. TitleAsync is the last enum entry before Count (gates.h:589), and {"KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC","titleasync",0,1} is the last KNOB_DEFINITIONS row (gates.cpp:402). The 'LAST row' comments moved correctly in both files.
Nothing else iterates knobs by count. Initialize, ScheduleOf and ApplyText in gates.cpp are the only loops, and all are sized Knob::Count. No test or static_assert pins the knob count.
The environment parse clamps KYTY_TITLE_ASYNC to 1 (the limit).

FindAssignment cannot confuse 'titleasync' with 'asyncsubmit', because a separator must precede the name. gen_gates.py's knob regex parses the new row. gates_base.txt (99 names) does not contain titleasync, so the knob keeps its compiled 0 in sealed runs.

FrameTrace-x: the four names pres_title_ns, pres_title_n, flip_rsv_wait_ns and flip_rsv_wait_n are appended after gw_idle_prio, which was the last entry in the parent commit (videoOut.cpp:2514 before, 2525-2528 after). They are printed including zeros. The names are unique in src, and no existing field moves. Scorers parse by name (RE_TOKEN / missing-field checks in shn113.py, vbn113f.py), so extra trailing fields cannot fail SCHEMA. LOGF uses fmt::sprintf into spdlog, with no length cap.
The Counter enum grows by 4 at the tail, before Count. The only Count-sized arrays are the Shard, retired and Snapshot arrays, all generic. The lean limit (index < LogNs) is unaffected.

Committed files have LF line endings (0 CR bytes in all six at HEAD). The net windowInternal.h change is 8 added lines: <string>, PostToMainThread, title_mutex, title_text, title_queued. build114a.log reports BUILD OK with no new warnings in the changed files.

info.title: flip_rsv_wait_n/_ns also count spin-only contention, not only blocking waits
info.failure: TryEnterCriticalSection fails on any contention, even a hold of a few ns by the vblank or status paths. EnterCriticalSection then spins up to its spin count and gets the lock without blocking. Such an acquisition is still counted in flip_rsv_wait_n and timed in flip_rsv_wait_ns. The frameStats.h:1870-1871 comment and ROADMAP say 'blocking waits'. The counter is therefore an upper bound on blocking events. It is still correct for the 3-s case the control targets.
info.fix: Describe it as 'contended acquisitions (spin + block)' in the counter comment and the scorer text. Code change optional.

info.title: KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST frame counts non-preparing UpdateTitle calls, not flip_status.count or FrameTrace n
info.failure: frame_num is UpdateTitle's own static counter. It advances only for presents with !preparing, and 'retry exhausted' drops skip it too. So '3000' is not FrameTrace n=3000. A seal-01 scorer that looks for the stall at FrameTrace n=3000 or n=3001 may miss it by the number of skipped presents.
info.fix: The seal-01 scorer should anchor on the 'MainStallTest: queued frame=' log line, or on the first FrameTrace line after it, not on a fixed n.

checked_ok: The sleep task is posted (window.cpp:1129) before the title task. At titleasync 0 the title ticket (RunOnMainThread :778-793) counts both posts because PostToMainThread also increments main_tasks_queued, and DrainMainThreadTasks runs the batch in FIFO order and adds tasks.size() to main_tasks_run. So the present thread waits about M ms plus one round trip, whether both tasks land in one batch or in two.
At titleasync 1 the present thread never waits. PostToMainThread only takes main_task_mutex and calls SDL_PushEvent, and neither is held by a main thread sleeping inside a task.
frame_num == stall_test.first: frame_num rises by exactly 1 per UpdateTitle call on the present thread only (never called while preparing), so the trigger fires exactly once.

On Windows, UpdateTitle is the only RunOnMainThread caller. swapchain.cpp:570 (RecreateSurface) is __APPLE__-only. No other flip-path, audio (SDL_QueueAudio / audio thread), input-script (HostInputKey, file poll) or overlay path (SDL_PushEvent, no wait) waits on the SDL main thread. So a sleep inside a task cannot freeze the emulation at titleasync 1 through the emulator's own code.
pres_title_ns does not include the stall-test post or its LOGF (title_t0 is taken after them, :1132).

Title slot at titleasync 1: title_mutex and main_task_mutex are never nested. There is no lost update: the task clears title_queued under the lock after reading the latest text, and the next UpdateTitle posts again. Switching the knob between 0 and 1 mid-run is safe, because the FIFO keeps the synchronous title task after any queued asynchronous one.

ReserveFlipRequest: TryLock then Lock is semantically identical to the old LockGuard (CRITICAL_SECTION, recursive). The RAII ReserveUnlock is built only after the lock is held and covers all three return paths after it. The early returns at :515-523 lock nothing.

No behaviour change at the default: titleasync=0 keeps the old RunOnMainThread path. The only additions are two NowNs calls, two Adds and one knob read per present. KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST unset means no post.

The knob tables match: TitleAsync is the last enum entry before Knob::Count and the last KNOB_DEFINITIONS row {env, name, fallback 0, limit 1}. Gates::Value initialises from the environment lazily through ValueSlow.

NowNs works without KYTY_FRAME_TRACE (rdtsc/QPC), so MainThreadWait timing is valid in untraced runs. The new counters print as raw ns/counts at the end of FrameTrace-x and work in lite mode (they are Add-based, not Scope-based).
Frame 3000 is reached in a Sky Garden entry: in vbn113m, FrameTrace n=3001 came at about 100 s from launch with stable at 17.9 s. It needs hold ≥ about 90 s after stable; the s113 seals used 300 s.
M=3000 is below the 8-s GpuHangAbort bound (4 two-second timeouts) and below the roughly 5-s Windows hung-window threshold.

info.title: flip_rsv_wait_* is not a clean present-hold or title indicator. MainThreadWait cannot fire at titleasync=1.
info.failure: ReserveFlipRequest counts every contended acquisition. That includes guest-thread CPU flips (VideoOutSubmitFlip, FlipRequestSource::Cpu) and short contention with VblankBegin/End, FlipQueue::Prepare and the guest's GetFlipStatus polling. Also, at titleasync=1 the present hold still covers acquire, the render-mutex wait, the submit, vkQueuePresentKHR and the logging. So flip_rsv_wait_ns stays above zero at both knob values, and a prediction of '→ 0 at titleasync=1' would fail. MainThreadWait times only the present thread's wait inside UpdateTitle. At titleasync=1 it measures a mutex plus SDL_PushEvent, so no MainThreadWait line is expected even while the main thread sleeps. pres_title_ns correctly EXCLUDES the stall-test post (title_t0 is taken after the post at :1129). At titleasync 0 it INCLUDES the whole main-thread batch in front of the title task, which is intended and is what makes the control work.
info.fix: Predict ABBA deltas for these counters, not zeros. Do not read 'no MainThreadWait at 1' as evidence.

info.title: In the titleasync=0 prediction, GpuWaitSlow is conditional, and M has two hard limits.
info.failure: At titleasync 0 the freeze is certain: the present thread blocks under cfg->mutex and vblanks stop. GpuWaitSlow, however, appears only if (a) a lazily unflushed EOP priority op is sitting on the recording tick when GuestGpu blocks in ReserveFlipRequest (usual, per prio_unsub ≈ 5.7 a frame, but not implied), and (b) the wait is in diagnostic mode (KYTY_QUEUE_TRACE / checkpoints / markers). A scorer that requires GpuWaitSlow can FAIL a correct control. Limits on M: with KYTY_GPU_HANG_ABORT_S=8 the priority thread EXITs with 'GPU stopped completing submissions' after about 8 s, a misattribution, so M must stay below about 7 s. At titleasync=1 the main thread pumps no window messages for M ms. Above about 5 s Windows marks the window hung (DWM ghosting). Any dependence of the driver or DWM present path on the message pump would then show up as a freeze with small pres_title_ns and be misread as the fix failing. M=3000 is inside both limits.
info.fix: Make GpuWaitSlow a secondary observable, not a requirement. Keep M=3000. Add KYTY_PRESENT_TRACE=1 to seal 01 so acquire_us/present_us around the injected frame can attribute any residual stall at titleasync=1.

info.title: After an injected stall, PresentThread fires a burst of about M/16.7 vblanks with no sleep. This already happens after any stall, but it will appear in the control rows.
info.failure: After a stall of M ms inside Flip, total_wait is about −M. Every later iteration with no Ready request returns from Flip(0) at once, skips the sleep (total_wait < 0), runs VblankBegin/VblankEnd, and pays back only one period. That gives about 180 vblank events (vblank_status.count++) within a few ms to seconds, interleaved with presents, as in vbn113k (the next present came 2.965 ms later). The rows after the stall therefore have tiny dt, and the guest sees a burst of vblanks at titleasync 0. A block-mean dt criterion understates the freeze and mixes in the catch-up.
info.fix: Score the freeze on the single stall row's dt, not on block means. Optionally clamp total_wait at −period in PresentThread; that is a separate knob, not part of this patch.

finding.title: The positive control can only confirm the knob works, not that the vbn113k 3-s blocker was the title wait. Once titleasync=1 ships, no instrument names a different blocker.
finding.failure: The control posts the sleep from inside UpdateTitle, the one path the knob changes. So seal 01 is certain to show 'freeze at 0, none at 1' whatever the real vbn113k blocker was. STALL_PATHS itself says the blocking call was never observed. Failure sequence: titleasync=1 ships, the 3-s stall recurs, and the row shows pres_title_ns small with flip_rsv_wait_ns about 3e9 in row n+1. That rules out the title but names nothing, because (a) MainThreadWait measures only the present thread's own wait and cannot fire at titleasync=1, (b) nothing measures how late the main thread was (no age of a posted task when it is drained, no 'last SDL event type' from STALL_PATHS §7(1)), and (c) the FlipHold split of the cfg->mutex hold (STALL_PATHS §7(2): Present / title / Gates::Poll / snapshot+log) was not built. A PASS of seal 01 plus the ABBA supports only 'titleasync=1 removes the RunOnMainThread wait'. It does not support 'the 3-s stall is fixed'.
finding.fix: Keep the claim at the knob level. Add a cheap FlipHold split: time the hold from videoOut.cpp:1148 to :2578 in phases and log lines over 50 ms naming the phase. Record the queue-to-run age of posted main-thread tasks in DrainMainThreadTasks, so a busy main thread stays visible at titleasync=1.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. Every factual part of the claim matches the code.

1. The control is tautological with respect to vbn113k. window.cpp:1126-1130 posts the sleep from inside UpdateTitle with PostToMainThread. At titleasync=0 the same call then goes into RunOnMainThread (window.cpp:1153). Its title task is queued behind the sleep, so DrainMainThreadTasks (window.cpp:808-822) runs the sleep first and only then signals the waiter (window.cpp:789-792). At titleasync=1 nothing waits. Seal 01 must therefore show "freeze at 0, none at 1" whatever blocked the present thread in vbn113k. It still tests one real thing: that a present-thread hold of about 3 s produces the GuestGpu block in ReserveFlipRequest and the GpuWaitSlow signature. It does not show that the main thread was busy in vbn113k. Both STALL_PATHS.md §0/§6 and ROADMAP §0.1 item 2 record M1 as "possible, blocking call NOT observed" and "main thread busy about 3 s, by what is not visible".

2. The instrument gaps are real:
   (a) MainThreadWait is logged only from UpdateTitle (window.cpp:1158-1165). At titleasync=1 the timed span is a title_mutex string swap plus PostToMainThread (a main_task_mutex push and SDL_PushEvent), so it cannot reach 50 ms in practice. The only other main-thread wait, swapchain.cpp:570, is `#if __APPLE__` and not timed.
   (b) DrainMainThreadTasks is unchanged. Nothing records how late a posted task ran or the last SDL event type, which STALL_PATHS §7(1) asked for.
   (c) The cfg->mutex hold, videoOut.cpp:1148 to 2578, is still unsplit. §7(2) FlipHold was not built. §7(3) was built only as the flip_rsv_wait counters, with no CfgMutexWait log line and no Prepare/GetFlipStatus sites.

3. The failure sequence is plausible. The hold after the present submit (swapchain.cpp:883-904, videoOut.cpp:1177-1250) also covers vkQueuePresentKHR, RenderDocOnGuestFlip, Gates::Poll, KernelSetGuestSpeed and the snapshot. On Windows, vkQueuePresentKHR can itself stall while the window-owning thread is not pumping messages. If the real blocker was any of these, titleasync=1 would not remove it. A recurrence would then show dt of about 3 s, a small pres_title_ns, and flip_rsv_wait_ns of about 3e9 in row n+1. That rules the title out and names nothing else. KYTY_PRESENT_TRACE=1 could split off present_us, but it is off by default and not in the seals.

The ROADMAP ships titleasync=1 as a "correctness fix" on the strength of this control plus the ABBA. That supports only "the knob removes the RunOnMainThread wait". This is not a code defect: nothing behaves wrongly, the default is unchanged, and the control does discriminate the knob's own mechanism. It is an attribution and instrument-completeness gap, so MINOR is the right severity.

I could not refute it. Every factual part of the claim checks out against the code at 36522d2/9d7712c.

1. **The control is injected on the path the knob changes.** In window.cpp:1126-1130, UpdateTitle calls PostToMainThread with a sleep of ms milliseconds when frame_num equals the configured frame. At titleasync 0, the RunOnMainThread wait that follows (window.cpp:1153, wait loop at :788-790) queues behind that sleep. At titleasync 1 (:1133-1151) nothing waits. So seal 01 shows "freeze at 0, none at 1" by construction. It checks the knob's mechanism. It cannot check whether the vbn113k blocker was the title. That is fine for a positive control, and the ROADMAP says so honestly (§СЕССИЯ 114 item 2: "M1 'возможно', блокирующий вызов НЕ наблюдался"; the ship bar is "не медленнее").

2. **(a) MainThreadWait cannot fire at titleasync 1.** At 1, UpdateTitle only takes title_mutex, which the main-thread task holds for a string copy. It then calls PostToMainThread (:796-805): main_task_mutex, which DrainMainThreadTasks holds only for a swap or increment, plus a non-blocking SDL_PushEvent. So title_ns never reaches 50 ms (:1158-1165).

3. **(b) Nothing measures how late the main thread is.** DrainMainThreadTasks (:807-821) records no queue-to-run age and no last SDL event type, although STALL_PATHS §7(1) proposed the event type.

4. **(c) The FlipHold split is not built.** FlipQueue::Flip holds cfg->mutex from videoOut.cpp:1148 to :2578. Nothing times Present, frames.Release, RenderDocOnGuestFlip, Gates::Poll (:1190) or the snapshot. The mh_pres_us counter only covers the render-mutex part of Present and is gated by mutsite, which gates_base pins to 0.

5. **Row booking is as described.** flip_rsv_wait_ns is added after Lock() returns (videoOut.cpp:525-529). That happens after the present thread unlocks at :2578, which is after row n's snapshot, so the wait lands in row n+1. pres_title_ns lands in row n.

**Partial mitigations, which narrow the gap but do not close it:**
- On Windows, UpdateTitle is the only synchronous present-to-main-thread dependency. The other RunOnMainThread call, in Swapchain::Recreate (swapchain.cpp:570), is Apple-only.
- So a recurrence at titleasync 1 with small pres_title_ns and flip_rsv_wait_ns near 3e9 would at least rule out the main thread.
- KYTY_PRESENT_TRACE (swapchain.cpp:884-892) could additionally split the hold at vkQueuePresentKHR.
- Even with both, the remaining candidates (frames.Release, Gates::Poll file I/O, the snapshot) are not named.

**Why MINOR and not MAJOR:**
- The code behaves correctly: default 0 keeps today's path, and the knob does what it says.
- The control does tell the two knob values apart.
- The patch implements exactly the instrument that ROADMAP item 2 recorded, and nothing in the code or ROADMAP claims the 3-s stall is fixed.

The defect is a real observability gap. vbn113k was a one-off event, so if it recurs after titleasync=1 ships, naming the blocker will need a new build plus a catch series. The cheap fix the reviewer proposes is well-founded: phase timers across the cfg->mutex hold with FlipHold lines above 50 ms, and the queue-to-run age of main-thread tasks.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the facts. The claim is still only a note on scope. The patch has no code defect here.

The code agrees with the reviewer:
- Presenter::Present (swapchain.cpp:838-909) runs all of these while the caller holds VideoOutConfig::mutex:
  - screenshot.Poll and input_script.Poll. InputScript::Poll calls std::filesystem::exists on _input.req every 8 presents (inputScript.cpp:169-171).
  - scheduler.Wait on the acquire tick, then acquireNextImageKHR with a UINT64_MAX timeout (:584-588).
  - RecoverSwapchain → Destroy → queue.waitIdle (:524-527).
  - The render mutex (:862), the present Submit, and queue_mutex + presentKHR (:721-722).
  - screenshot.Finish.
  - UpdateTitle, which is the only piece the patch changes.
- VblankBegin and VblankEnd run on the same PresentThread around Flip(0) (videoOut.cpp:829/865 area). So a long hold also stops vblanks.
- RunOnMainThread has only two callers. One is swapchain.cpp:570, inside #if defined(__APPLE__). The other is window.cpp:1153, UpdateTitle. So on Windows, UpdateTitle really is the only main-thread round trip on the flip path.
- The patch changes nothing but UpdateTitle, the ReserveFlipRequest timing and the counters. Any other slow call inside the hold can still strand GuestGpu at ReserveFlipRequest, before the flip's Flush. The "stall class still open" statement is therefore true by construction.

Why it is not MAJOR, and I would rate it INFO:
(1) Nothing behaves wrongly. The knob does what ROADMAP §0.1 session 114 item 2 decided: fix (a) of STALL_PATHS §6.
(2) STALL_PATHS.md, which ROADMAP item 2 cites, already lists (b) "do not hold cfg->mutex across Present / Gates::Poll" and (c) "flush before PrepareVideoOutFlip" as separate fixes. It already names Gates::Poll file I/O as the "second suspect". It already says the blocking call was NOT observed.
(3) docs/next-session-114.md "Must not be claimed" forbids claiming the stall's cause is known before the site is caught.
(4) The new instruments separate the cases if the stall recurs. At titleasync=1, a large flip_rsv_wait_ns with a small pres_title_ns and no MainThreadWait line points at a blocker other than the title.

The "second limit" does not hold up:
- The guest calls PadSetLightBar, PadSetVibration and SetTriggerEffect take SDL_LockJoysticks on guest threads, not on the flip path under cfg->mutex. They cannot produce the GuestGpu-stranded-before-flush stall that this patch targets.
- The sleep task in KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST is meant to show that the knob removes the title-path wait, and it does that: 0 waits, 1 does not. It was never meant to model every way the main thread can be busy.

What remains valid is a documentation point. ROADMAP item 2 describes the ship as a "correctness fix" for the 3-s stall, but does not say that (b) and (c) stay open. It should say that titleasync=1 closes only the title path.

I could not refute the finding. Its factual claims hold, but it describes the limited scope of the patch, not a defect in it.

What I checked in the code:
- FlipQueue::Flip takes r.cfg->mutex at videoOut.cpp:1148 and releases it at :2578. Inside that hold are:
  - m_presenter.Present
  - RenderDocOnGuestFlip (:1179)
  - Gates::Poll (:1190)
  - VulkanLogMemoryStats every 300 flips (:1245)
  - the FrameTrace LOGF block
  - TriggerVideoOutEvents (:2572)
- Presenter::Present (swapchain.cpp:838-909) makes these calls under that hold:
  - ScreenshotGrabber::Poll and InputScript::Poll. Each runs std::filesystem::exists on a relative request file every 8 presents (inputScript.cpp:169-171, screenshot.cpp:250-255), and the working directory is the OneDrive emulator folder.
  - AcquireNextImage, which does present_scheduler.Wait and acquireNextImageKHR with a UINT64_MAX timeout (:584-588).
  - RecoverSwapchain. Destroy() does DrainAsyncSubmits plus queue.waitIdle (:524-528), and the RunOnMainThread at :570 is inside #if __APPLE__.
  - the render-mutex LockGuard (:862).
  - the present Submit.
  - queue_mutex plus presentKHR (:721-722).
  - screenshot.Finish.
  - UpdateTitle.
- The patch changes only UpdateTitle. The new PostToMainThread is used only there and in the stall test. A repo-wide grep finds RunOnMainThread called only at swapchain.cpp:570 (Apple-only) and window.cpp:1153 (the titleasync=0 branch). So "on Windows, UpdateTitle is the only RunOnMainThread caller on the flip path" is correct.
- VblankBegin and VblankEnd run on the same PresentThread around Flip(0) (videoOut.cpp:839-875), so a long hold also stops vblanks.
- The guest pad calls do go through SDL_GameControllerFromInstanceID (controller.cpp:747/778/792/822).

Where the list is weaker than stated:
- Item 6, the render mutex, cannot strand GuestGpu in ReserveFlipRequest. For the present thread to wait on the render mutex, GuestGpu must be holding it inside a draw, so GuestGpu is not in ReserveFlipRequest at that moment. It is ordinary serialisation, and a slow compile there freezes GuestGpu itself.
- Items 3-5, 7 and 8 are GPU/driver waits, and items 1, 2 and 11-13 are OS/file-system waits, bounded by the OS. None of them is an unbounded wait on another emulator thread. The removed UpdateTitle→RunOnMainThread round trip was one.
- The point about SDL joystick locks is about guest pad calls, not the cfg->mutex hold.
- The sleep-in-a-task control still discriminates titleasync 0 from 1 on the title path, which is all it is designed and planned to show. So this is not a "control that cannot discriminate" defect.

Why the severity is INFO:
- The patch does exactly what it and ROADMAP item 2 describe, and it changes nothing at the default.
- The session documents already hedge. ROADMAP item 2 says the blocking call was not observed ("блокирующий вызов НЕ наблюдался"). next-session-114.md forbids claiming the stall's cause is known before the site is caught. STALL_PATHS.md §6 lists fixes (b) and (c) as separate and notes that (c) alone does not remove the hitch.

The real residue is documentation: ROADMAP item 2 does not record that (b), unholding cfg->mutex across Present, Gates::Poll and logging, and (c), flushing before PrepareVideoOutFlip, stay open after titleasync=1 ships. Adding that note, as the finding proposes, is appropriate. It is not a behavioural defect in 36522d2.

finding.title: frame= in MainStallTest/MainThreadWait counts presents, not FrameTrace n. The seal has to find the stall row by log order and must admit a run only if the trigger fired.
finding.location: src/graphics/presentation/window/window.cpp:1081,1095,1126-1129; swapchain.cpp:903; videoOut.cpp:858-873 (blank presents before video-out open), :1169-1175 (held flips skip Present)
finding.failure: UpdateTitle runs once per successful Present with !preparing. That includes the blank presents between the end of shader preparation and VideoOutOpen (about 1 s, roughly 60 presents in the vbn113m timeline) and paused or overlay re-presents. It excludes AsyncPipelines-held flips. In vbn113m (same scene): FrameTrace n=3 at 8.79 s, n=397 at 17.4 s (the stable point), n=3001 at 99.99 s. So 'queued frame=3000' fires near FrameTrace n of about 2940, about 80 s after stable. Failure sequences: (1) a scorer keyed on the row n=3000/3001 reads a normal row, giving a false FAIL at titleasync 0. (2) With --hold under about 90 s, or with KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST lost (the known trap: shell-exported KYTY_* are dropped by enter_scene.py unless passed positionally), the trigger never fires and the titleasync=1 arm passes 'no freeze' by default. The equality test itself is correct: frame_num rises by exactly 1 per call, so it fires once. Note that frame=0 never fires. Also, the knob value set through the environment leaves no log line, and MainThreadWait prints titleasync= only when it fires (only at 0), so the log cannot confirm which arm a titleasync=1 run was on.
finding.fix: In the seal: take the stall row to be the first 'FrameTrace: n=' line after 'MainStallTest: queued'. The present thread writes both, in order, in the same FlipQueue::Flip. Require the 'MainStallTest: frame=3000 ms=3000' and 'queued' lines in BOTH runs. Use a hold of at least 120 s after stable. Log the knob value once, for example as a 'TitleAsync: mode N' line on the first UpdateTitle.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The code confirms the counting mismatch, and the patch's own spec describes the trigger in the terms the reviewer warns about.

1) What `frame=` counts. In window.cpp, UpdateTitle keeps a function-static `frame_num` (window.cpp:1081). It is incremented on every call (:1095) before the trigger comparison at :1126. The only caller is swapchain.cpp:903, `if (!preparing) m_impl->window.UpdateTitle();`, which runs after every successful Presenter::Present. That includes blank presents while no video-out is open (videoOut.cpp:858-873) and overlay re-presents (:841-856). FrameTrace n is a different counter: it is `r.cfg->flip_status.count`, incremented in FlipQueue::Flip after the present (videoOut.cpp ~1187) and printed at :1269. Held incomplete flips go to `m_presenter.Discard` (:1174), so they increment flip_status.count and never call UpdateTitle. The two counters therefore drift apart in both directions.

2) The run length checks out. log_vbn113m.txt runs at dt_us ≈ 33 000 (about 30 fps). FrameTrace n=3000 and n=3001 appear at log lines 503822/503842, so present 3000 falls near 100 s. A shorter hold means the trigger never fires. Nothing in the code guards against that; only the absence of the `MainStallTest: queued` line shows it.

3) The spec invites the wrong key. ROADMAP.md:1613-1617 says "на кадре N ... (строка кадра с dt ≈ M)", i.e. it describes the trigger as a frame row. A scorer written from that text would plausibly key on the row FrameTrace n=3000.

4) The suggested anchor works. At titleasync 0 the sleep task is queued first. The RunOnMainThread title task is queued behind it on the same queue in the same present, so the wait happens inside that Present. The FrameTrace row printed right after it, in the same Flip, carries the stall. So "first FrameTrace after `MainStallTest: queued`" is the correct way to find the row.

5) Minor sub-claims:
- frame=0 can never fire, because the increment comes before the compare. This is trivial.
- A knob set through the environment is not logged (gates.cpp:421-433). This is true, but it applies to every knob, not just this one. A gate-file assignment does log `Gate: titleasync=1 frame=N` (gates.cpp:581), and that is the harness's normal route.

Why MINOR and not higher: the patch code behaves correctly, and the control can tell the arms apart as long as the seal anchors on the `queued` line and requires it in both runs. The defect is that the spec's wording and the code's semantics disagree, which is a trap for the not-yet-written seal scorer. It is not wrong runtime behaviour.

I could not refute this. The core claim holds in the code.

- `frame_num` is a function-local static in `WindowContext::UpdateTitle` (window.cpp:1081). It goes up once per call (window.cpp:1095) before the check at window.cpp:1126. Because the increment comes first, `frame=0` can never fire. The trigger fires exactly once, when `frame_num == N`.
- `UpdateTitle` is called only from `Presenter::Present`, after a successful present, when `!preparing` (swapchain.cpp:903). `PresentThread` calls `Present` for more than guest flips: paused re-presents (videoOut.cpp:829-831), overlay refreshes (videoOut.cpp:839-854), and blank frames while no video-out handle is open (videoOut.cpp:856-873).
- Held incomplete flips call `m_presenter.Discard` rather than `Present` (videoOut.cpp:1169-1176). They still increment `flip_status.count` (videoOut.cpp:1188).
- `FrameTrace: n=` prints `r.cfg->flip_status.count` (videoOut.cpp:1277).

So `MainStallTest: queued frame=N` counts successful non-preparing presents, not the FrameTrace row number.

In vbn113m there are no `held (incomplete` lines, and shader preparation ends at log line 4285, well before the first FrameTrace row (18109). Blank presents can only add to `frame_num`, so the trigger fires at FrameTrace n ≤ 3000, not at n=3000/3001. The ROADMAP §0.1 text for this session says "на кадре N ... строка кадра с dt ≈ M", which invites a scorer keyed on n. The trigger lands about 80 s after the scene is stable (~30 fps), so a short hold misses it. A scorer that does not require the `queued` line would then pass the titleasync=1 arm with no stall to test.

The fix works: `UpdateTitle` runs inside `Present`, which is inside `FlipQueue::Flip` before the FrameTrace print. The first `FrameTrace: n=` after `queued` is therefore the stall row, and its dt contains the ~3 s wait at titleasync 0.

One part of the claim is overstated. When the arm is set through `KYTY_GATE_FILE` (how the harness normally sets arms), the change is logged as `Gate: titleasync=1 frame=...` (gates.cpp:581). Only the environment route is silent, and that is true for every existing knob.

Severity is MINOR, not MAJOR. The control can tell the arms apart when scored as proposed; the defect is a counter whose meaning is not documented, plus a trap for the seal that has not been written yet.

finding.title: One injected stall lands in two different FrameTrace rows: pres_title_ns in row n, flip_rsv_wait_ns (and the priority semwait) in row n+1.
finding.failure: The present thread adds pres_title_ns in UpdateTitle, inside Present (videoOut.cpp:1177), before the row-n snapshot at :1247-1251, so row n carries about 3e9. GuestGpu's blocking Lock at :528 returns only after the present thread unlocks at :2578, which is after row n has been printed. So FlipReserveWaitNs/N go into row n+1, like the 2.975-s semwait in vbn113k (STALL_PATHS F5). A scorer that looks for pres_title_ns≈M AND flip_rsv_wait_ns≈M in the same row always sees one of them near 0 and calls the titleasync=0 arm not reproduced.
finding.fix: In the preregistration, score pres_title_ns and dt on the stall row n, and flip_rsv_wait_ns and GpuWaitSlow/semwait on row n+1. Or sum over the pair.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. The code does what the claim says.

Present thread, in FlipQueue::Flip (videoOut.cpp):
- It takes r.cfg->mutex at :1148 and calls m_presenter.Present(*r.frame) at :1177.
- Present leads to swapchain.cpp:903 `if (!preparing) m_impl->window.UpdateTitle();`.
- At the end of UpdateTitle (window.cpp, the added block after the RunOnMainThread branch), FrameStats::Add(PresTitleNs, title_ns) runs on the present thread's shard.
- flip_status.count++ follows at :1187, then the snapshot at :1248-1251. FS::Read (frameStats.cpp:214-223) sums every live shard under the registry mutex, so row n already carries pres_title_ns of about M. Its dt_us, cur.host_ns - prev.host_ns, also includes the stall.
- After row n and its FrameTrace-x/-draw/site lines are printed, m_mutex.Unlock() and r.cfg->mutex.Unlock() run at :2577-2578.

GuestGpu side, in ReserveFlipRequest (videoOut.cpp:526-535): after a failed TryLock it blocks in video_out->mutex.Lock() at :528. Lock returns only after :2578, and only then does it Add FlipReserveWaitNs/N. Row n has already been read by then, so the whole wait is booked in row n+1.

- **A late Add is not plausible.** It could only miss row n+1 if GuestGpu were descheduled for a whole present between Lock returning and its Add.
- **The logs already show this split.** In vbn113k (STALL_PATHS F3/F5), row 9672 has dt_us=3032310 and the 2.975-s semwait sits in row 9673.

Why only INFO and not MINOR:
- **Nothing in the patch behaves wrongly.** Each counter lands where its Add site puts it.
- **The failure needs a scorer that does not exist yet.** It assumes one that requires pres_title_ns≈M and flip_rsv_wait_ns≈M in the same row. Seal 01's scorer is not written; C:/kyty/s114 holds only stall/, the build log and the exe.
- **The recorded prediction already scores the right row.** ROADMAP.md:1615 predicts, in its own words, "the row of the frame with dt ≈ M, GpuWaitSlow at M > 2000" (строка кадра с `dt` ≈ M, `GpuWaitSlow` при M > 2 000). dt and pres_title_ns both sit in row n, so the control can still tell the two arms apart.
- **The project already documents this trap** (STALL_PATHS F5).

The point is still worth writing into the seal-01 preregistration: score dt_us and pres_title_ns on row n, and flip_rsv_wait_ns and semwait on row n+1, or sum over the pair.

A related pitfall for the same scorer: UpdateTitle's own frame_num (window.cpp static, which KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST and MainThreadWait frame= use) counts every non-preparing Present. That includes the overlay-refresh and blank presents at videoOut.cpp:843/854/872. So it is not FrameTrace n (flip_status.count), and the scorer should not locate the stall row by n==3000.

I could not refute it. The code puts the two counters in different rows.

1. The present thread takes r.cfg->mutex at videoOut.cpp:1149 and calls m_presenter.Present at :1177. On the same thread, Present reaches swapchain.cpp:903, which calls UpdateTitle. With titleasync 0, window.cpp:1126-1129 first posts the stall task. Then title_t0 is taken and RunOnMainThread waits behind the sleep. PresTitleNs (about M) is added at window.cpp:1153-1154. The row-n snapshot comes later on that thread (FS::Read loop right after NoteFrame, about :1247-1251), so row n carries pres_title_ns ≈ 3e9. It also carries dt ≈ M, because cur.host_ns is taken after Present.

2. In ReserveFlipRequest (videoOut.cpp:526-531), GuestGpu fails TryLock and blocks in video_out->mutex.Lock(). That is the same config mutex. It returns only after the present thread's r.cfg->mutex.Unlock() at :2578, which comes after row n has been snapshotted and printed. FlipReserveWaitNs/N are added only after Lock returns, so they cannot be in row n.

3. The reviewer says the wait lands in row n+1. That understates it. Common::Mutex is a CRITICAL_SECTION (threads.cpp:178, :306), which is not FIFO-fair. If flip n+1 is already Ready, the present thread can take the mutex again for flip n+1 before the woken GuestGpu does. The Add then lands in row n+2, and its value also includes the present time of n+1. So summing over the pair {n, n+1} is not always enough; a window n..n+2 is safer.

4. This matches the observed precedent: STALL_PATHS F3/F5 booked the 2.975-s semwait in row 9673, not 9672.

Why MINOR, not MAJOR: this is a scoring and preregistration hazard, not wrong emulator behaviour. The planned prediction in ROADMAP.md:1614-1616 only scores dt ≈ M on the stall row, plus a GpuWaitSlow log line. Both are consistent with row n: dt and pres_title_ns share row n. A scorer written to that plan would not be misled. A scorer that also requires flip_rsv_wait_ns ≈ M on the same row would always fail the titleasync 0 arm, as the finding says. No seal-01 scorer exists yet in C:/kyty/s114, so the fix is to preregister the row mapping: pres_title_ns and dt on row n, flip_rsv_wait_ns and semwait on rows n+1..n+2.
